checklist.title: Verify Trust Boundary Integrity: Is receipt type-prefix byte strictly validated to {1, 2, 3, 4} in decode_receipt?

reachability.notes: A malicious peer could send a receipt with an invalid type-prefix byte via devp2p. The assertion is the primary gatekeeper.

checklist.test_procedure: 1. Locate the decode_receipt function in the RLP codec module. 2. Identify where the first byte (type-prefix) of the receipt is extracted and validated. 3. Verify that validation explicitly checks receipt[0] is in {1, 2, 3, 4}. 4. Craft test receipts with type-prefix bytes 0x00, 0x05, 0xFF and confirm decode_receipt reverts/fails for each. 5. Test edge cases: empty receipt (no bytes), single-byte receipt with invalid prefix. 6. Trace the P2P ingestion path to confirm decode_receipt is invoked before any state updates.
checklist.notes: Source: PROP-0004, Trust Boundary: tb-026, Pre-condition for decode_receipt. Bypassing this check could allow state corruption or consensus divergence.

checklist.title: Verify P2P peer cannot inject receipts with invalid type-prefix bytes

reachability.notes: A malicious peer could send a receipt with an invalid type-prefix byte via devp2p. The assertion is the primary gatekeeper.

checklist.test_procedure: 1. Set up a test environment with a devp2p connection to the execution client. 2. Craft a malformed receipt message with type-prefix byte = 0x00 and send via P2P. 3. Verify the node rejects the receipt and does not incorporate it into state. 4. Repeat with type-prefix bytes 0x05, 0x06, 0x7F, 0x80, 0xFE, 0xFF. 5. Monitor for any error handling that might silently accept invalid receipts. 6. Check that the peer sending invalid data is appropriately penalized or disconnected.
checklist.notes: Source: PROP-0004, Actor boundary: actor-p2p-peer to actor-execution-client. PoC guidance: craft receipt with type-prefix outside {1,2,3,4} and demonstrate rejection.

checklist.title: Verify RLP codec assertion fails for all invalid receipt type-prefix values

reachability.notes: A malicious peer could send a receipt with an invalid type-prefix byte via devp2p. The assertion is the primary gatekeeper.

checklist.test_procedure: 1. Review the actor-rlp-codec implementation of decode_receipt. 2. Enumerate all 256 possible first-byte values (0x00-0xFF). 3. Verify that only values {0x01, 0x02, 0x03, 0x04} are accepted. 4. For each invalid value, confirm an assertion failure or explicit error is raised. 5. Check for off-by-one errors in range checks (e.g., < 5 instead of <= 4). 6. Verify no fallback/default case silently accepts unknown types.
checklist.notes: Source: PROP-0004, Invariant: blocks-SG-002-INV-001. Pre-condition type property - design test to bypass with invalid inputs.

checklist.title: Verify Trust Boundary Integrity: Is the receipt type prefix byte stripped correctly (exactly 1 byte) before RLP decoding?

reachability.notes: Incorrect offset in byte stripping would cause RLP decoding to fail or produce corrupt receipt data.

checklist.test_procedure: 1. Locate the decode_receipt function implementation in the execution client. 2. Verify that exactly one byte (receipt[0]) is stripped before passing to RLP decoder. 3. Confirm the slice operation is receipt[1:] and not receipt[0:], receipt[2:], or any other offset. 4. Test with receipts having type prefixes {1, 2, 3, 4} and confirm correct byte stripping for each. 5. Verify the invariant: decode_receipt(receipt) == rlp.decode_to(Receipt, receipt[1:]) holds. 6. Check for any conditional logic that might strip different numbers of bytes based on type prefix.
checklist.notes: Source: PROP-0005, Source Invariant: blocks-SG-002-INV-002, Trust Boundaries: tb-026, tb-027. Off-by-one in prefix stripping corrupts all receipt decoding.

checklist.title: Verify RLP Codec Boundary: Does data flow from execution client to RLP codec correctly strip type prefix?

reachability.notes: Incorrect offset in byte stripping would cause RLP decoding to fail or produce corrupt receipt data.

checklist.test_procedure: 1. Trace data flow from actor-execution-client to actor-rlp-codec across trust boundaries tb-026 and tb-027. 2. Verify that the byte slice passed to rlp.decode_to starts at index 1 (receipt[1:]). 3. Test edge cases: minimum valid receipt length, receipt with exactly 2 bytes (prefix + minimal RLP). 4. Fuzz the receipt deserialization path with malformed inputs to detect off-by-one errors. 5. Verify error handling when prefix stripping produces invalid RLP data. 6. Check for integer overflow in slice index calculations.
checklist.notes: Source: PROP-0005, Covered Nodes: actor-execution-client, actor-rlp-codec. Boundary edge between P2P layer and internal RLP processing.

checklist.title: Can consensus splits occur due to inconsistent receipt prefix stripping across client implementations?

reachability.notes: Incorrect offset in byte stripping would cause RLP decoding to fail or produce corrupt receipt data.

checklist.test_procedure: 1. Review the invariant: forall (receipt : Bytes, receipt[0] in {1,2,3,4}): decode_receipt(receipt) == rlp.decode_to(Receipt, receipt[1:]). 2. Attempt to falsify by finding inputs where stripping != 1 byte produces different but valid-looking results. 3. Test with boundary values: receipt[0] = 1 (EIP-2930), receipt[0] = 2 (EIP-1559), receipt[0] = 3 (EIP-4844), receipt[0] = 4 (Fusaka type). 4. Compare decoding behavior across different client implementations (Geth, Nethermind, Besu, Erigon) to verify consensus compatibility. 5. Create a PoC demonstrating that incorrect byte stripping causes different decoded receipt data. 6. Verify that all clients produce identical Receipt structs from identical input bytes.
checklist.notes: Source: PROP-0005, Severity Justification: Off-by-one in prefix stripping corrupts all receipt decoding, causing consensus splits between clients that decode differently. PoC: demonstrate that decode_receipt strips an incorrect number of bytes before RLP decoding.

checklist.title: Verify Trust Boundary Integrity: Are encode_receipt and decode_receipt exact inverse operations for all typed transactions?

reachability.notes: If encode and decode are not exact inverses, data transmitted between peers via P2P will be corrupted, causing network partitions.

checklist.test_procedure: 1. Identify all typed transaction receipt formats supported by the system (EIP-2930, EIP-1559, EIP-4844, Fusaka types). 2. For each transaction type, create valid receipt objects with edge-case values (empty fields, maximum values, special characters in logs). 3. Execute encode_receipt followed by decode_receipt on each test receipt. 4. Assert strict equality between original and roundtripped receipt objects using deep comparison. 5. Test with receipts containing optional fields present and absent. 6. Test with receipts at RLP encoding boundaries (e.g., values crossing single-byte/multi-byte thresholds like 0x7F to 0x80). 7. Verify no data loss or transformation occurs during the roundtrip for all field types.
checklist.notes: Source: PROP-0007, Trust Boundaries: tb-026, tb-027, tb-029. Invariant type: forall (tx, receipt): decode_receipt(encode_receipt(tx, receipt)) == receipt. PoC requirement: demonstrate a receipt where encode followed by decode produces a different receipt object.

checklist.title: Supporting Check: Does the RLP codec correctly handle all receipt field types without lossy transformations?

reachability.notes: If encode and decode are not exact inverses, data transmitted between peers via P2P will be corrupted, causing network partitions.

checklist.test_procedure: 1. Review actor-rlp-codec implementation for encode_receipt and decode_receipt functions. 2. Identify all field types within receipts: status (uint8), cumulativeGasUsed (uint64), logsBloom (256 bytes), logs (array of Log structs). 3. For each field type, verify the encoding preserves type information and exact values. 4. Check for implicit type coercions or normalizations that could cause data drift (e.g., leading zero handling in integers). 5. Test BigInt handling at uint256 boundaries (0, 2^64-1, 2^256-1). 6. Verify log topic and data encoding preserves exact byte sequences without padding or truncation. 7. Check bloom filter encoding/decoding for bit-exactness across all 2048 bits.
checklist.notes: Source: PROP-0007, Covered Node: actor-rlp-codec. Supporting check for primary boundary verification. Focus on RLP codec internal correctness.

checklist.title: Supporting Check: Does the execution client correctly process receipts received from P2P peers after decode?

reachability.notes: If encode and decode are not exact inverses, data transmitted between peers via P2P will be corrupted, causing network partitions.

checklist.test_procedure: 1. Trace receipt flow from P2P reception through execution client processing to storage. 2. Verify execution client uses decoded receipts without additional transformations that could mask roundtrip issues. 3. Test that receipts decoded from P2P messages match locally-generated receipts for the same transactions. 4. Check for any normalization or canonicalization applied after decoding that could hide encode/decode mismatches. 5. Verify receipt root computation uses identical receipt representations across encode/decode boundary. 6. Test receipt retrieval via eth_getTransactionReceipt to ensure stored receipts match original decoded receipts.
checklist.notes: Source: PROP-0007, Covered Node: actor-execution-client. Supporting check for primary boundary verification. Focus on execution client receipt handling.

checklist.title: Supporting Check: Are receipts transmitted between P2P peers byte-identical after encode-transmit-decode cycle?

reachability.notes: If encode and decode are not exact inverses, data transmitted between peers via P2P will be corrupted, causing network partitions.

checklist.test_procedure: 1. Set up two P2P peers with receipt exchange capabilities via devp2p. 2. Generate a comprehensive set of test receipts with varying complexity on peer A covering all transaction types. 3. Transmit encoded receipts from peer A to peer B via Receipts message. 4. On peer B, decode received receipts and re-encode them. 5. Compare byte representations: sha3(original_encoded) must equal sha3(re_encoded). 6. If any difference is detected, this indicates a non-invertible encode/decode operation. 7. Test with receipts from all supported transaction types including EIP-2718 typed transactions and future Fusaka types. 8. Include receipts with maximum-length logs and edge-case bloom filter values.
checklist.notes: Source: PROP-0007, Covered Node: actor-p2p-peer. Supporting check for primary boundary verification. Critical for preventing network partitions and consensus splits.

checklist.title: Verify Trust Boundary Integrity: Is the Withdrawal data structure properly frozen and immutable after construction at the Engine API boundary?

reachability.notes: Withdrawals originate from the consensus layer via Engine API. A compromised CL could send malformed withdrawal instructions.

checklist.test_procedure: 1. Identify the Withdrawal struct definition and locate the slotted_freezable implementation. 2. Trace all code paths where Withdrawal objects are constructed from Engine API payloads (newPayload, forkchoiceUpdated). 3. Verify that freeze() is called immediately after all four fields (index, validator_index, address, amount) are set. 4. Attempt to mutate any field after the freeze operation and verify rejection. 5. Check for any reflection, unsafe, or serialization paths that could bypass immutability. 6. Verify no partial construction paths exist where freeze is called before all fields are set. 7. Test with malformed withdrawal data from a simulated compromised consensus layer.
checklist.notes: Source: PROP-0008, Trust Boundary: tb-024, Invariant: blocks-SG-003-INV-001. Mutable withdrawal objects could be tampered with after construction, leading to unauthorized ETH credits.

checklist.title: Verify Withdrawal Field Completeness: Are all four required fields validated before freeze operation?

reachability.notes: Withdrawals originate from the consensus layer via Engine API. A compromised CL could send malformed withdrawal instructions.

checklist.test_procedure: 1. Review the Withdrawal constructor and builder patterns. 2. Verify that index (U64), validator_index (U64), address (Address), and amount (U256) are all validated for proper types and ranges before freeze. 3. Test construction with missing fields and verify rejection. 4. Test with zero values, max values, and boundary values for each field. 5. Verify address field is validated as a proper 20-byte Ethereum address. 6. Check that amount cannot overflow U256 bounds during any calculations.
checklist.notes: Source: PROP-0008, Supporting check for field completeness validation. Source Assumption: asm-034.

checklist.title: Verify Consensus Layer to Execution Client Withdrawal Handoff: Is withdrawal data integrity preserved across the actor boundary?

reachability.notes: Withdrawals originate from the consensus layer via Engine API. A compromised CL could send malformed withdrawal instructions.

checklist.test_procedure: 1. Trace the withdrawal data flow from consensus layer (actor-consensus-layer) to execution client (actor-execution-client). 2. Verify JWT authentication is enforced on the Engine API endpoint receiving withdrawals. 3. Check that withdrawal data is re-validated on the execution client side, not trusted blindly from CL. 4. Test with replayed withdrawal requests to ensure idempotency or proper rejection. 5. Verify withdrawal objects cannot be modified during transit or after receipt. 6. Check for race conditions between withdrawal receipt and freeze operation.
checklist.notes: Source: PROP-0008, Covers actors: actor-execution-client, actor-consensus-layer. Edge: tb-024.

checklist.title: Verify Trust Boundary Integrity: Are all Withdrawal fields validated as non-None before freeze operation at Engine API boundary?

reachability.notes: Partial withdrawal construction could lead to undefined behavior when serialized or processed.

checklist.test_procedure: 1. Identify the Withdrawal data structure and its freeze() operation at the Engine API boundary (tb-024). 2. Locate all code paths where Withdrawal objects are constructed from external input via Engine API. 3. Verify that validation explicitly checks: w.index != None, w.validator_index != None, w.address != None, w.amount != None BEFORE freeze() is called. 4. Attempt to construct a Withdrawal with each field individually set to None and verify that freeze() is rejected or fails safely. 5. Check for race conditions where fields could be unset between validation and freeze. 6. Verify error handling paths do not allow partial withdrawals to propagate to block processing. 7. Test with null/undefined values in JSON payloads from Engine API to verify rejection.
checklist.notes: Source: PROP-0009, Trust Boundary: tb-024, Source Invariant: blocks-SG-003-INV-002, Source Assumption: asm-033. Pre-condition: forall (w : Withdrawal): freeze(w) requires w.index != None AND w.validator_index != None AND w.address != None AND w.amount != None. PoC: demonstrate that a Withdrawal with a missing field can be frozen and used in block processing.

checklist.title: Verify Execution Client validates Withdrawal field completeness before forwarding to Consensus Layer processing

reachability.notes: Partial withdrawal construction could lead to undefined behavior when serialized or processed.

checklist.test_procedure: 1. Trace data flow from actor-execution-client to actor-consensus-layer for Withdrawal objects. 2. Identify serialization points where incomplete Withdrawal could cause undefined behavior. 3. Verify that the execution client rejects or sanitizes Withdrawals with missing fields before passing to consensus layer. 4. Test with malformed Engine API payloads containing partial Withdrawal structures (missing index, validator_index, address, or amount). 5. Monitor for crashes, panics, or unexpected behavior when processing edge cases. 6. Verify that incomplete withdrawals cannot reach the SSZ serialization layer.
checklist.notes: Source: PROP-0009, Nodes: actor-execution-client, actor-consensus-layer, Primary Element: SG-003 (withdrawal_construction). Partially constructed withdrawals could cause undefined behavior or crashes during serialization.
